photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white with colour); photographic print
photo.reason: A Tohono O'odham (Papago) woman is shown making pottery outdoors beside traditional adobe/ocotillo structures, surrounded by pots and coiled baskets characteristic of the Sonoran Desert region; this is a documentary/postcard photo of traditional craft and daily life.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white); photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary photo postcard captioned "Typical Papago Indian Home near Tucson, Arizona," showing a traditional O'odham dwelling with a woman and baskets under a ramada — directly matches the claimed Tohono O'odham (Papago) ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: Museum description explicitly identifies the sitter as "Luis Morago, a Papago man" — Papago being the historical name for the Tohono O'odham — photographed in a Hayden Survey-era studio portrait wearing a woven cloth wrapped around his head over a Western suit; this is a documentary ethnographic photo of an O'odham individual, matching the claimed group despite the stray "Pima" caption on the card (a common period mislabel among related O'odham peoples).

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Luis Morago, identified as a Papago (Tohono O'odham) man, with plaited hair, photographed in Washington D.C.—a documentary photograph of an actual tribal member, which fits the "documentary photos... in any photographic style" allowance even though he wears Western dress.
